answer: To weather a gale of fake identities, an agent marketplace requires every identity to lock 100 tokens for a 30-day horizon before bidding. The kernel of its defense is a public escrow contract that rejects bids without that deposit and slashes it for cryptographically proven double-signing of exclusive commitments. An attacker running 1,000 identities must immobilize 100,000 tokens, paying financing costs even if none are caught cheating.
